title: A step that died
summary: A program killed by a signal is DIED, not FAILED: killedBy n, exit 128+n, and the plan stops whatever onFail says. The report the LLM is sent: History, Job, State, Stage reached, each step PASS/FAIL/DIED/NOT RUN, the error point (first error-pattern line of stderr, else the end of stderr, else the end of stdout: what it was doing when it died) with 3 lines before and 6 after, and relative paths of the full logs for ws~tail. Live: killall -9 make mid-compile gave "make was killed by signal 9 (SIGKILL)", last stdout line sleep 3.
authority: built and tested (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: The LLM is sent the error point and a trace, never the full output
A died step stops the plan
procedure: When stderr is empty, look at the end of stdout

provenance.claim: kill mid-compile, DIED, SIGKILL, sleep 3 in the report
